sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普林，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每晚你都要带上300件你最珍爱的藏品去上班，你把一个DJ台变成了一个像是由美丽的50年历史老物件组成的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: A series of blockbuster hearings from the January 6th Committee is putting growing pressure on the Attorney General, Merrick Garland,
sentences.zh: 来自1月6日调查委员会的一系列重磅听证会，正对司法部长梅里克·加兰施加越来越大的压力，

sentences.en: to bring criminal charges against former President Trump for his role in inciting violence at the Capitol and trying to overturn the election.
sentences.zh: 要求对前总统特朗普在煽动国会山暴力事件以及试图推翻选举中所起的作用提起刑事指控。

sentences.en: Today, as the committee prepares for its latest hearing on Thursday night,
sentences.zh: 今天，正当委员会为周四晚上的最新听证会做准备时，

sentences.en: my colleague Mike Schmidt talks to one of the prosecutors who led the last major investigation into Trump about why bringing and winning a case against the former president is such a challenge.
sentences.zh: 我的同事迈克·施密特采访了一位领导了上一场针对特朗普重大调查的检察官，探讨为什么对这位前总统提起诉讼并赢得官司是如此巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月21日，星期四。

sentences.en: They usually don't let me do this, so this is like, uh, we're good?
sentences.zh: 他们通常不让我做这个，所以这就像是……呃，我们这样可以吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Okay, it's weird to hear my own voice through my...
sentences.zh: 好吧，通过我的……听到自己的声音感觉好怪。

sentences.en: You got a bit of a radio voice.
sentences.zh: 你有点广播员的嗓音。

sentences.en: I do not think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是对的。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Uh, before we start, tell us who you are.
sentences.zh: 呃，在我们开始之前，先告诉我们你是谁。

sentences.en: Like, who are you?
sentences.zh: 比如，你到底是谁？

sentences.en: Why, what have you done in your career?
sentences.zh: 为什么，你在职业生涯中做过什么？

sentences.en: Oh, well, early in my career, I was a writer for Time Magazine.
sentences.zh: 哦，嗯，在我职业生涯的早期，我是《时代周刊》的撰稿人。

sentences.en: I decided to become a lawyer, and early in that career, I was a federal prosecutor in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我决定成为一名律师，在那个职业生涯的早期，我是曼哈顿的一名联邦检察官。

sentences.en: I focused on public corruption cases.
sentences.zh: 我专注于公众腐败案件。

sentences.en: I became the chief of the public corruption unit at a time when we brought successful cases against several major New York political figures.
sentences.zh: 我成为了公共腐败部门的主管，当时我们成功起诉了几位纽约的重要政治人物。

sentences.en: But then I was asked to join the Mueller investigation, and I moved to Washington and worked on that for two years.
sentences.zh: 但后来我被邀请加入穆勒调查，我搬到了华盛顿并为此工作了两年。

sentences.en: And now I'm the head of the white-collar practice at the law firm Cooley.
sentences.zh: 现在我是高卫律师事务所白领犯罪业务的负责人。

sentences.en: You're not someone that, um, that I know that well.
sentences.zh: 你不是那种……嗯，我那么熟知的人。

sentences.en: I mean, during the Mueller investigation, I showed up at your house to try and get you to talk.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在穆勒调查期间，我出现在你家门口，试图让你开口说话。

sentences.en: And I went to your door, and your doorbell was broken, and we knocked on the door, and I could hear you and your family inside.
sentences.zh: 我走到你门口，你的门铃坏了，我们敲了门，我能听到你和你的家人在里面。

sentences.en: And I was with a colleague of mine, and I turned to the colleague, and I said,
sentences.zh: 我和我的一个同事在一起，我转向同事，然后我说，

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: This is too invasive.
sentences.zh: 这太侵犯隐私了。

sentences.en: We've gone too far.
sentences.zh: 我们太过分了。

sentences.en: This man is inside with his family, and we left.
sentences.zh: 这个人正和家人待在里面，然后我们就离开了。

sentences.en: Um, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道这件事。

sentences.en: That's all a little creepy.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: It's fair.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Totally fair.
sentences.zh: 完全没错。

sentences.en: I first came to know the name Andrew Goldstein in the course of my own reporting on the Mueller investigation.
sentences.zh: 我最初得知安德鲁·戈尔茨坦这个名字，是在我对穆勒调查进行自己的报道的过程中。

sentences.en: The thing is, is that this is an issue you understand.
sentences.zh: 关键是，这是一个你能够理解的问题。

sentences.en: In journalism, we often talk about people being the foremost expert on something.
sentences.zh: 在新闻界，我们经常谈论某人是某领域的头号专家。

sentences.en: But because of his work on the Mueller investigation, Goldstein is literally one of the last federal prosecutors to look at the question of whether Donald Trump broke the law.
sentences.zh: 但由于他在穆勒调查中的工作，戈尔茨坦实际上是最后几位审查过特朗普是否触犯法律这一问题的联邦检察官之一。

sentences.en: And so over the past few weeks, as the January 6th committee has presented all of its evidence about Trump's behavior in the lead up to and during January 6th,
sentences.zh: 因此，在过去的几周里，随着1月6日委员会提交了关于特朗普在1月6日之前及当天行为的所有证据，

sentences.en: And as my editors have come to me literally every day to ask me,
sentences.zh: 而且随着我的编辑们几乎每天都来问我，

sentences.en: Did Trump break the law, and will or won't the Attorney General Merrick Garland bring charges against him?
sentences.zh: 特朗普到底有没有违法？司法部长梅里克·加兰会不会对起他提起指控？

sentences.en: The only person I wanted to answer those questions was Andrew Goldstein.
sentences.zh: 我唯一想要回答这些问题的人就是安德鲁·戈尔茨坦。

sentences.en: On the obstruction investigation, we looked at whether or not President Trump...
sentences.zh: 在妨碍司法公正的调查中，我们调查了特朗普总统是否……

sentences.en: We started our conversation by talking about his experience on the Mueller investigation.
sentences.zh: 我们的对话从探讨他在穆勒调查中的经历开始。

sentences.en: The two-year-long inquiry that looked at ties between Russia and Trump's 2016 campaign.
sentences.zh: 那项历时两年的调查审视了俄罗斯与特朗普2016年竞选团队之间的联系。

sentences.en: But you concentrated in the Mueller investigation on a narrow question, an important question, but a narrow question of whether Trump had tried to impede that investigation, right?
sentences.zh: 但你在穆勒调查中集中精力于一个狭窄的问题，一个重要但狭窄的问题，即特朗普是否曾试图阻挠那项调查，对吗？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what did you find?
sentences.zh: 你们发现了什么？

sentences.en: As we noted in our report,
sentences.zh: 正如我们在报告中所指出的，

sentences.en: we found that the president's conduct during the course of the investigation involved a series of actions that involved attacking the investigation publicly,
sentences.zh: 我们发现总统在调查期间的行为包含了一系列动作，包括公开攻击调查，

sentences.en: and privately, and privately, trying to control the investigation from his position as president and within the White House.
sentences.zh: 以及私下里，私下里试图以总统的身份和在白宫内部来控制这项调查。

sentences.en: There were efforts in both public and private to encourage witnesses not to cooperate with the investigation.
sentences.zh: 在公开和私下都有努力鼓励证人不配合调查。

sentences.en: And so those were our predominant findings in terms of obstruction.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我们关于妨碍司法方面的主要调查结果。

sentences.en: And despite finding all of these things that, at the very least, was not great behavior,
sentences.zh: 尽管发现了所有这些至少算不上好的行为，

sentences.en: you made a decision about what to do about whether Trump broke the law.
sentences.zh: 你对是否就特朗普违法采取行动做出了一项决定。

sentences.en: What was that decision?
sentences.zh: 那是什么决定？

sentences.en: Well, ultimately, we decided not to do what traditional prosecutors do when they're considering bringing a criminal charge.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最终，我们决定不去做传统检察官在考虑提起刑事指控时会做的事情。

sentences.en: We went down that road for a few different reasons.
sentences.zh: 我们走上那条路是基于几个不同的原因。

sentences.en: It was based on our understanding of the role of the president and our understanding of what we believe to be the proper role of a prosecutor.
sentences.zh: 这是基于我们对总统角色的理解以及我们对检察官应有职能的理解。

sentences.en: So, you guys basically made a decision not to make a decision, to sort of let the facts speak for themselves and say,
sentences.zh: 所以，你们基本上做出了一个不作决定的决定，有点像是让事实不言自明，并说，

sentences.en: look, if after this man, Donald Trump, leaves office and the Justice Department wants to prosecute him, they can do that based on what we found.
sentences.zh: 看，在这位名叫唐纳德·特朗普的男子离任后，如果司法部想起诉他，他们可以根据我们的发现来这样做。

sentences.en: But we're not going to make a decision.
sentences.zh: 但我们不会做出决定。

sentences.en: We're not going to say whether we think he broke the law.
sentences.zh: 我们不会说明我们是否认为他违反了法律。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's basically right.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上是这样。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that, you know, normally the first step that a prosecutor takes
sentences.zh: 原因在于，你知道的，通常检察官在决定对某人提起刑事指控时采取的第一步，

sentences.en: when deciding to bring a criminal charge against somebody is to determine for yourself whether that person is, in fact, guilty.
sentences.zh: 是为自己确定此人是否确实有罪。

sentences.en: And then you weigh the admissible evidence.
sentences.zh: 然后你权衡可采纳的证据。

sentences.en: You see, you know, can you actually prove this case in court?
sentences.zh: 你看，你知道的，你真的能在法庭上证明这个案件吗？

sentences.en: Will it stand up on appeal?
sentences.zh: 它经得起上诉吗？

sentences.en: But here, we weren't dealing with an ordinary subject.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，我们面对的不是一个普通的涉案对象。

sentences.en: You know, the president is the head of the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 你知道，总统是行政部门的负责人。

sentences.en: Under Department of Justice policy, the president cannot be charged with a crime while in office.
sentences.zh: 根据司法部的政策，总统在任期间不能被指控犯罪。

sentences.en: And that is because simply charging him with a crime, just making the accusation, that would infringe on his ability to be president.
sentences.zh: 这是因为仅仅指控他犯罪，仅仅提出指控，就会侵犯他担任总统的能力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that leads us to the January 6th hearings and a different set of circumstances, because, of course, Trump is no longer president.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们引向了1月6日的听证会和一套不同的情况，因为当然，特朗普已经不再是总统了。

sentences.en: Explain to me what crimes Donald Trump could be investigated for, based on everything we've learned from the January 6th hearings.
sentences.zh: 请向我解释，根据我们从1月6日听证会了解到的所有情况，唐纳德·特朗普可能会因哪些罪行而被调查。

sentences.en: I think the three main potential crimes that people have talked about and that would be at issue here are, number one, obstruction of an official proceeding.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们一直在谈论且会成为这里核心问题的三个主要潜在罪行是：第一，妨碍官方程序。

sentences.en: Number two, conspiracy to defraud the United States.
sentences.zh: 第二，阴谋欺诈美国。

sentences.en: And number three, depending on the evidence, seditious conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 第三，根据证据而定的煽动性阴谋。

sentences.en: Let's start with seditious conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 让我们从煽动性阴谋开始。

sentences.en: What does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: And how hard is that to prove?
sentences.zh: 这有多难证明？

sentences.en: It means agreeing with one or more other people to use force or violence to prevent the law from being carried out.
sentences.zh: 这意味着与一个或多个人达成一致，使用武力或暴力来阻止法律的实施。

sentences.en: Some of the people who stormed the Capitol on January 6th have been charged with this and it's for their efforts and their plans to stop the counting of the electoral vote by force.
sentences.zh: 1月6日冲进国会山的一些人已经被以此罪名起诉，这是因为他们试图通过武力阻止选举人票的清点。

sentences.en: So basically using violence to stop the certification of the election.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上就是使用暴力来阻止选举结果的认证。

sentences.en: So for someone like Trump to be charged with that, would that mean that the government would have to prove that he conspired with those individuals to use violence?
sentences.zh: 因此，要让像特朗普这样的人被控此罪，是否意味着政府必须证明他与那些个人密谋使用暴力？

sentences.en: Would you have to show that he told them to commit violence?
sentences.zh: 你是否必须证明他指示他们实施暴力？

sentences.en: Would you have to show that he actually committed violence himself?
sentences.zh: 你是否必须证明他自己实际实施了暴力？

sentences.en: You would not have to show that he committed violence himself.
sentences.zh: 你不需要证明他自己实施了暴力。

sentences.en: You'd have to show that he agreed with people who were going to use violence or who were planning to use violence to stop the electoral vote count from happening.
sentences.zh: 你必须证明他与那些打算使用暴力或计划使用暴力以阻止选举人票清点的人达成了一致。

sentences.en: So you basically need like Donald Trump sitting down with the Oath Keepers and with like a map of the Capitol and saying, look,
sentences.zh: 所以你基本上需要唐纳德·特朗普和“誓言守护者”坐在一起，拿着一张国会山的地图说，看，

sentences.en: like this is how you guys should break into the building to stop Pence from doing his certification.
sentences.zh: 就像你们应该这样闯入大楼来阻止彭斯进行认证一样。

sentences.en: I don't think you need that much, but you need to be able to prove that the president had an agreement or that he joined a conspiracy to not just have the vote count be stopped,
sentences.zh: 我认为不需要那么多，但你需要能够证明总统达成了协议，或者他加入了一个阴谋，不仅是为了让投票计票停止，

sentences.en: but to use force or violence to stop it.
sentences.zh: 而且是为了使用武力或暴力来阻止它。

sentences.en: And the evidence is out on the public record right now, I don't think would support that.
sentences.zh: 目前公开记录上的证据，我认为并不支持这一点。

sentences.en: Okay, so what about the charge of defrauding the public, defrauding the American people?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么关于欺诈公众、欺诈美国人民的指控呢？

sentences.en: It seems like just from watching it that there might be a lot of grist for a charge there.
sentences.zh: 光是看着这些，似乎就会有很多构成这项指控的素材。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of Trump's efforts to install loyalists at the Justice Department,
sentences.zh: 我想到的是特朗普试图在司法部安插忠信之士的努力，

sentences.en: him pressuring the Secretary of State of Georgia to come up with the exact number of votes that he needed to win that state.
sentences.zh: 他向佐治亚州州务卿施压，要求得出他在该州取胜所需的准确选票数。

sentences.en: It certainly looks to many like he took these acts knowing that he lost the election but was still trying to overturn them anyway.
sentences.zh: 在许多人看来，这当然像是他在明知自己输掉选举的情况下仍然采取这些行动，却无论如何都要推翻它们。

sentences.en: Are those examples of actions that could be used to show that he was defrauding the American people?
sentences.zh: 这些是可以用来证明他一直在欺诈美国人民的行为的例子吗？

sentences.en: Look, there is a crime called conspiracy to defraud the United States,
sentences.zh: 听着，有一项罪名叫做阴谋欺诈美国，

sentences.en: and it effectively means conspiring or agreeing with other people where the intent is to stop or obstruct the lawful function of the government using deceitful or dishonest means.
sentences.zh: 它实际上意味着与其他人密谋或达成协议，其意图是使用欺骗或不诚实的手段来阻止或妨碍政府的合法职能。

sentences.en: He says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: For many watching the hearings, it might seem like that charge describes Trump's behavior in the period leading up to January 6th.
sentences.zh: 对于许多观看听证会的人来说，这项指控似乎描述了特朗普在1月6日之前那段时间的行为。

sentences.en: Because with the help of the little-known lawyer John Eastman, Trump tried to come up with a scheme that would essentially overthrow the election.
sentences.zh: 因为在鲜为人知的律师约翰·伊斯特曼的帮助下，特朗普试图炮制一个基本上能推翻选举的计划。

sentences.en: And they did that based on a lie, that there was election fraud.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做是基于一个谎言，即存在选举舞弊。

sentences.en: After all, Trump had been told many times, including by his own Attorney General Bill Barr, that there was no election fraud.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，特朗普曾多次被告知，包括被他自己的司法部长威廉·巴尔告知，根本没有选举舞弊。

sentences.en: Goldstein says there is probably enough evidence to bring that kind of charge.
sentences.zh: 戈尔茨坦表示，可能有足够的证据提出这种指控。

sentences.en: But he also says...
sentences.zh: 但他也表示……

sentences.en: The difficulty with that kind of a charge here is that it's a little novel.
sentences.zh: 这里这种指控的难点在于它有点新颖。

sentences.en: Conspiracy to fraud is something that's not itself novel, but applying it to this set of facts, as I've seen it, is something that has not clearly been done before.
sentences.zh: 欺诈阴谋本身并不是一个新概念，但正如我所看到的，将它应用到这套事实上，是以前没有明确做过的事情。

sentences.en: It would be an unusual use of the law.
sentences.zh: 这将是对法律的一种不寻常的使用。

sentences.en: And when you're a prosecutor, you don't want to test-run novel legal charges against a former president.
sentences.zh: 当你是一名检察官时，你不会想拿前总统来测试新颖的法律指控。

sentences.en: In short, bringing the charge of conspiracy to defraud the United States would be far riskier and more difficult than pursuing the third charge Trump could face,
sentences.zh: 简而言之，提出阴谋欺诈美国的指控将比追究特朗普可能面临的第三项指控要危险得多、困难得多，

sentences.en: obstructing a congressional proceeding.
sentences.zh: 第三项指控是妨碍国会程序。

sentences.en: Well, then let's get to that third charge, the charge of obstructing an act of Congress.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我们来谈谈第三项指控，即妨碍国会法案的指控。

sentences.en: Define that for us.
sentences.zh: 为我们定义一下。

sentences.en: The proceeding itself would be the proceeding on January 6th, where Congress and the vice president were going to certify the results of the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 程序本身将是1月6日的程序，当时国会和副总统要对2020年选举结果进行认证。

sentences.en: And the crime would be doing something or conspiring with others to do something to obstruct that proceeding and to do it corruptly.
sentences.zh: 而罪行将是做某事或与他人密谋做某事以妨碍该程序，并且是以腐败的方式去做的。

sentences.en: How would you prove that someone obstructed an act of Congress or a congressional proceeding?
sentences.zh: 你将如何证明某人妨碍了国会法案或国会程序？

sentences.en: At the most basic level, you need two things.
sentences.zh: 在最基础的层面上，你需要两样东西。

sentences.en: You need some action that would impede or would tend to impede the proceeding itself.
sentences.zh: 你需要某种会阻碍或倾向于阻碍程序本身的行动。

sentences.en: And then you need corrupt intent.
sentences.zh: 然后你需要腐败的意图。

sentences.en: Intent is typically the hardest thing to show in a political corruption or in an obstruction investigation.
sentences.zh: 在政治腐败或妨碍司法调查中，意图通常是最难证明的事情。

sentences.en: It requires showing that somebody was acting with an improper motive, that he was effectively conscious of wrongdoing at the time he took his action.
sentences.zh: 它需要证明某人的行为带有不正当的动机，即他在采取行动时实际上意识到自己是在做坏事。

sentences.en: And here, there's been a lot of evidence about the president's advisors and lawyers and people from the Department of Justice telling the president that the election was over,
sentences.zh: 在这里，有很多证据表明总统的顾问、律师以及来自司法部的人员告诉总统选举已经结束，

sentences.en: that there wasn't sufficient evidence of fraud to overturn the results of the election.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的证据证明存在足以推翻选举结果的欺诈行为。

sentences.en: And so that's the kind of evidence that would get at the president's intent as he's continuing to push these claims of fraud even after having been told all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那种能够探究总统意图的证据，因为他在被告知这一切之后，依然继续推销这些欺诈的主张。

sentences.en: But there's evidence that he was told that Mike Pence did not have the power to, on his own,
sentences.zh: 但有证据表明，他被告知迈克·彭斯没有权力独自一人

sentences.en: refuse to take part in the certification or to delay the certification of the votes and that he continued to push Pence to do that.
sentences.zh: 拒绝参与认证或推迟对选票的认证，但他继续敦促彭斯这样做。

sentences.en: And then there's the evidence of his conduct on January 6th itself and some of the things he did not do while it was clear that the Capitol had been effectively under siege and people were telling him to take actions and he didn't.
sentences.zh: 然后还有他在1月6日当天行为的证据，以及当国会山显然实际上处于围困状态、人们告诉他采取行动而他却没有采取时，他没有做的一些事情。

sentences.en: All of those are things that would go to helping establish the president's intent.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是有助于确立总统意图的事情。

sentences.en: Okay, so there's some evidence that could help establish intent here.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以有一些证据可以帮助在这里确立意图。

sentences.en: But as you said, as a prosecutor, you would want to establish intent and action.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，作为一名检察官，你会想要确立意图和行动。

sentences.en: What would be, putting the facts aside, which we're not supposed to do in journalism, what would a clear-cut example be of an action?
sentences.zh: 撇开事实不谈——我们在新闻工作中不该这么做——行动的一个明确例子会是什么？

sentences.en: If I said make up an action that shows obstructing a congressional proceeding, what would that look like?
sentences.zh: 如果我说编造一个表现出妨碍国会程序的行动，那会是什么样子的？

sentences.en: And I think, like, if, for example,
sentences.zh: 我想，比如，

sentences.en: if there was evidence that the president directed Mike Pence's security detail to not let Pence go to the Capitol or when he was there to actually direct them to get him out of there before he could certify the vote,
sentences.zh: 如果有证据表明总统指示迈克·彭斯的安保团队不要让彭斯去国会山，或者当他在那里时直接指示他们在彭斯认证选票之前把他弄出去，

sentences.en: that would be an act.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个行动。

sentences.en: It would absolutely have the effect of impairing or impeding the proceeding.
sentences.zh: 它绝对会产生削弱或阻碍程序的效果。

sentences.en: And I think if that was what happened, I think it wouldn't be that hard to show that the intent was corrupt.
sentences.zh: 我想如果那是发生的事情，我认为要证明其腐败意图并不那么难。

sentences.en: So you need a clear-cut example of Trump doing something that literally impedes this certification.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要一个明确的例子，证明特朗普做了某事，字面意思上阻碍了这项认证。

sentences.en: Not necessarily in that you could have an attempt or you could have a conspiracy, but in the end, I think a prosecutor would still need to point to an act,
sentences.zh: 不一定非得是你可以有未遂或阴谋，但最后，我认为检察官仍然需要指出一个行为，

sentences.en: an action that the president either took himself or directed to have been taken that would itself obstruct the proceeding.
sentences.zh: 一个总统自己采取或指示采取的、其本身就会妨碍程序的行动。

sentences.en: Based on what we know,
sentences.zh: 根据我们所了解的，

sentences.en: Trump tried to pressure Pence in the days leading up to January 6th to essentially take the certification into his own hands and either decide who won or send the votes back to the states.
sentences.zh: 在1月6日之前的几天里，特朗普曾试图向彭斯施压，实质上是让他把认证选举结果的事大权独揽，要么由他自己决定谁赢了，要么把选票退回给各州。

sentences.en: You have Trump's actions on the ellipse, where he gives a speech and he says, let's all march to the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 我们看看特朗普在椭圆形广场的举动，他在那里发表了一场演讲，并说，让我们一起向国会大厦进发。

sentences.en: And then he tries to go there himself in his own motorcade.
sentences.zh: 然后他试图自己坐着车队去那里。

sentences.en: And then when the riot is going on, Trump tweets about Pence, criticizing Pence for how Pence did.
sentences.zh: 接着，当骚乱发生时，特朗普在推特上针对彭斯，指责彭斯表现不佳。

sentences.en: Unpack those different acts and explain to us why those different acts would potentially get you there or not get you there in terms of establishing that Trump did something to truly impede the proceeding.
sentences.zh: 请剖析这些不同的行为，并向我们解释为什么这些不同的行为可能会或者不会让你得出结论，即特朗普确实采取了某些行动来真正阻碍程序的进行。

sentences.en: I think for each of those acts, there are ways to look at them where they would, in fact, have had the tendency to obstruct the proceeding, but they all have their own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于这些行为中的每一项，都有办法从某种角度看待它们，它们确实会产生妨碍程序的倾向，但它们各自都有各自的问题。

sentences.en: For example, if the jawboning of Pence is basically a disagreement and he's not trying to actually stop the proceeding,
sentences.zh: 例如，如果对彭斯的劝说基本上只是一种分歧，而他并不是真的想阻止程序的进行，

sentences.en: he's trying to get the proceeding to come out in a way that's in his favor or hope that, you know, by going up there and then getting delayed, it could buy him some time.
sentences.zh: 他只是想让程序朝着对他的有利方向发展，或者希望，你知道的，通过走到那里然后被拖延，可以为他争取一些时间。

sentences.en: That's different than an action that could actually obstruct the proceeding.
sentences.zh: 这与真正能够妨碍程序的行动是不同的。

sentences.en: And the other things that you mentioned and that are out there, the speech that the president gave on the ellipse early that afternoon,
sentences.zh: 还有你提到的以及外界存在的其他事情，总统那天下午早些时候在椭圆形广场发表的演讲，

sentences.en: telling the Secret Service to take away the magnetometers, the tweet about the vice president when people were already inside the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 命令特勤局撤走金属探测器，以及在人们已经进入国会大厦时发出的关于副总统的推特。

sentences.en: These are things where, on the one hand,
sentences.zh: 这些事情一方面，

sentences.en: you can make an argument that they were designed to try to rile people up to then be able to go to the Capitol and to obstruct the proceeding.
sentences.zh: 你可以提出这样一种论点，即它们的目的是激起人们的情绪，以便随后能够前往国会大厦并阻碍程序的进行。

sentences.en: But there are also things that politicians generally do, and there's a defense that this is political speech, that the tweet would be political speech,
sentences.zh: 但这也是政客们通常会做的事情，并且存在这样一种辩护，即这是政治言论，那条推特将是政治言论，

sentences.en: that the only reason he would have said to not let the magnetometers stay up would be because he wanted to pack the crowd and nothing to do with trying to get people who were armed to then go to the Capitol.
sentences.zh: 他之所以会说不让金属探测器保留，唯一的理由是因为他想让集会人满为患，而这与试图让携带有武器的人去国会大厦没有任何关系。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that because these actions that he took are sort of braided together with his First Amendment rights,
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，因为他所采取的这些行动与他的第一修正案权利交织在了一起，

sentences.en: it makes it more difficult for those to be actual acts because it's unclear where sort of his free speech rights begin or end and his intent to obstruct the proceeding picks up from there.
sentences.zh: 这使得这些行动更难被视为实质性行为，因为目前尚不清楚他的言论自由权利从哪里开始或结束，而他阻碍程序进行的意图又是从哪里开始介入的。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: I think when it comes in particular to the speech itself and to the tweet or other tweets, that those,
sentences.zh: 我认为当具体谈到演讲本身以及那条推特或其他推特时，对于那些，

sentences.en: he would have a legal argument that it's core protected First Amendment activity.
sentences.zh: 他将拥有一个法律论据，即这是核心受保护的第一修正案活动。

sentences.en: He's the president.
sentences.zh: 他是总统。

sentences.en: He needs to be able to talk to supporters.
sentences.zh: 他需要能够与支持者对话。

sentences.en: He didn't explicitly say, let's go march on the Capitol and break the doors down and stop this proceeding from happening.
sentences.zh: 他并没有明确地说，让我们去国会大厦游行，把大门砸烂，并阻止这个程序发生。

sentences.en: And so there's a real legal defense there.
sentences.zh: 因此，那里存在一个真实的法律辩护。

sentences.en: And factually, there's the defense that he did not, in fact, sort of say the magic words that would be true incitement.
sentences.zh: 在事实上，也存在这样一种辩护，即他实际上并没有说出构成真正煽动言论的魔幻词汇。

sentences.en: At least he would have an argument that that's not what he was actually doing.
sentences.zh: 至少他会有一个论点，即这并不是他当时真正在做的事情。

sentences.en: So if I'm reading between the lines on what you're saying, it seems like in terms of these two things you need, intent and an act,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我在字里行间揣摩你的意思，似乎就你所需要的这两点而言，即意图和行为，

sentences.en: based on what we know and has come out at the hearings, there's probably enough on the intent side.
sentences.zh: 根据我们所了解的以及在听证会上披露的情况，在意图方面可能已经足够充分了。

sentences.en: But on the act side, it's fuzzier in terms of whether there's a clear cut act.
sentences.zh: 但在行为方面，是否存在明确的行为则更加模糊。

sentences.en: Is that, I mean, if we're sitting back and we're assessing this and you're saying, okay, just do it for us, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果我们坐在这里进行评估，而你说，好吧，就帮我们做这件事，对吧？

sentences.en: So like, you're the prosecutor, how much, you know, do you get there on, on each one?
sentences.zh: 所以，就像你是检察官一样，你知道，你在每一项上掌握了多少证据？

sentences.en: Number one, I don't really want to weigh in on the strength of the evidence in part because I don't know all of it.
sentences.zh: 第一，我真的不想对证据的强度发表意见，部分原因是我并不知道全部证据。

sentences.en: And it would be a little bit of shooting from the sidelines to weigh in.
sentences.zh: 而且在场外发表意见会有点像是隔岸观火。

sentences.en: But number two, I do think it's important as the evidence is coming out of the January 6th committee to realize that there are difficulties here in proving either of these things.
sentences.zh: 但第二，随着1月6日委员会的证据不断披露，我确实认为认识到证明这两点中的任何一点都存在困难是很重要的。

sentences.en: There are issues with, are any of the things that the president did or tried to get others to do that day, would they really count as obstructive acts?
sentences.zh: 这里存在这样的问题：总统那天所做的事情或试图让其他人做的事情，是否真的能算作妨碍性行为？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in terms of his intent, there's definitely been a lot of evidence that has come out.
sentences.zh: 就他的意图而言，确实有很多证据浮出水面。

sentences.en: Does that get you over the hump of proving beyond a reasonable doubt that the president was acting with a corrupt intent?
sentences.zh: 这是否能让你跨过“排除合理怀疑”的门槛，证明总统行事时怀有腐败的意图？

sentences.en: I think these are very hard questions.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些都是非常棘手的问题。

sentences.en: Beyond the obvious of like, you know, wanting to have witnesses in the room for everything and documents backing it all up.
sentences.zh: 除了显而易见的事情之外，比如，你知道的，希望每个环节都有证人在场，并且有文件作为全面支撑。

sentences.en: If you were the prosecutor here, what would you want to know?
sentences.zh: 如果你是这里的检察官，你会想知道什么？

sentences.en: What would you really be keying in on to try and understand whether the president broke the law?
sentences.zh: 你真正会把重点放在哪里，试图弄清楚总统是否触犯了法律？

sentences.en: One thing that I think I would want to know, is there any evidence that the president was telling people internally, anybody internally,
sentences.zh: 我想知道的一件事是，是否有任何证据表明总统曾在内部对人们说，对任何内部人员说，

sentences.en: that he didn't believe the things he was saying, that he knew he had lost, and that all of this was effectively a construct to try to stay in power.
sentences.zh: 他不相信自己所说的话，他知道自己已经输了，这一切实际上只是为了继续掌权而构建的一个借口。

sentences.en: If the department had evidence of him saying that to a confidant or to somebody who was in the inner circle,
sentences.zh: 如果司法部门掌握了他对密友或核心圈子里的人说过这样话的证据，

sentences.en: that's the kind of evidence that I think if I were a prosecutor in this type of a case, I would really want.
sentences.zh: 这就是我认为如果我是这种案件的检察官真正想要的证据。

sentences.en: And why does that change things?
sentences.zh: 为什么这会改变情况？

sentences.en: I think it goes right at the heart of intent, and it would put a very strong gloss on all of the actions that have already come out through this January 6th committee process.
sentences.zh: 我认为这直接触及了意图的核心，并且会为通过这次1月6日委员会程序已经披露的所有行动赋予一个非常强有力的解释。

sentences.en: So you're saying by strengthening intent, it sort of helps to bolster the acts because their intentions of the actual acts are clear.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，通过强化意图，它在某种程度上顺带有助于支撑这些行为，因为实际行动的意图变得清晰了。

sentences.en: Because I think what it could end up showing is that some of the actions might be able to be read in different ways.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这最终可能会表明，其中一些行动可能会被以不同的方式解读。

sentences.en: If the government could actually show that the reason behind them, the intent behind them, was all about trying to stop the certification of the election,
sentences.zh: 如果政府能够实际证明其背后的原因、背后的意图，全都是为了试图阻止对选举结果的认证，

sentences.en: that would then change what might be the type of act that could be read in two different directions,
sentences.zh: 那么这就会改变那种原本可能被双向解读的行为类型，

sentences.en: and read in a way where actually that's the kind of action where the purpose of it was to impede the certification of the election.
sentences.zh: 并将其解读为这样一种行动：其目的就是为了阻碍选举结果的认证。

sentences.en: So bolstering one can help bolster the other.
sentences.zh: 所以，强化一方面可以帮助强化另一方面。

sentences.en: It can.
sentences.zh: 确实可以。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商业、政治和文化领域一些最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上对精选采访进行现场直播，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，你可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得我们所有新闻报道的一个月免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过它的。

sentences.en: After our last hearing, President Trump tried to call a witness in our investigation, a witness you have not yet seen in these hearings.
sentences.zh: 在我们上一次听证会后，特朗普总统试图给我们的调查中的一位证人打电话，这位证人你尚未在这些听证会上见过。

sentences.en: That person declined to answer or respond to President Trump's call and instead alerted their lawyer to the call.
sentences.zh: 该人员拒绝接听或回应特朗普总统的来电，而是将这通来电告知了他们的律师。

sentences.en: Their lawyer alerted us.
sentences.zh: 他们的律师通知了我们。

sentences.en: And this committee has supplied that information to the Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 并且本委员会已将该信息提供给了司法部。

sentences.en: Let me say one more time, we will take any effort to influence witness testimony very seriously.
sentences.zh: 请让我再说一次，我们对待任何试图影响证人证词的企图都极其严肃。

sentences.en: We've heard Liz Cheney talk about witness tampering.
sentences.zh: 我们听过利兹·切尼谈论干预证人作证的行为。

sentences.en: Would a witness tampering charge here be more appealing to a prosecutor?
sentences.zh: 在这里，指控干预证人作证是否对检察官更有吸引力？

sentences.en: It's potentially because it's more straightforward than some of the other things that are out there.
sentences.zh: 有可能，因为它比现有的其他一些指控更直接。

sentences.en: It's easier for the public to digeSt.
sentences.zh: 公众更容易消化。

sentences.en: And the law on witness tampering is very clear.
sentences.zh: 而且关于干预证人作证的法律非常明确。

sentences.en: You're not going to be pushing for some aggressive view of the law.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去推行某种激进的法律观点。

sentences.en: Like, I do think factually tying the former president to the type of witness tampering that came up in that congressional hearing, I think, would be a challenge.
sentences.zh: 就像我确实认为，在事实上将前总统与那场国会听证会中出现的干预证人作证行为联系起来，我认为将是一个挑战。

sentences.en: What Goldstein told me is that for a witness tampering charge to stick,
sentences.zh: 戈尔茨坦对我说的是，要让干预证人作证的罪名成立，

sentences.en: a prosecutor would have to prove that Trump himself was involved in the outreach to witnesses and that he intended to prevent the witnesses from testifying or from testifying truthfully.
sentences.zh: 检察官必须证明特朗普本人参与了对证人的接触，并且他意图阻止证人作证或阻止证人如实作证。

sentences.en: He said, while the evidence of outreach presented by the committee is concerning, it doesn't prove that Trump was trying to interfere in witness testimony.
sentences.zh: 他说，虽然委员会提出的接触证据令人担忧，但它并不能证明特朗普当时正试图干预证人证词。

sentences.en: But if that were the provable crime,
sentences.zh: 但如果那是可以被证明的罪行，

sentences.en: that in some ways becomes easier to explain that no person can tamper with a witness as they're going to provide testimony before Congress on an important issue.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面，这就变得更容易解释了，即任何人不得在证人准备就重大议题在国会作证时对其进行干预。

sentences.en: So it's cleaner and clear if the facts support it.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果事实支持的话，它会更干净利落、更清晰。

sentences.en: I think it would be both cleaner and clear.
sentences.zh: 我认为它既会更干净利落，也会更清晰。

sentences.en: OK, so let's say if prosecutors think they can prove intent, they think they have an act, an action,
sentences.zh: 好的，那么假设如果检察官认为他们能够证明意图，他们认为自己掌握了一个行为、一项行动，

sentences.en: and they think they can prove the count beyond a reasonable doubt and they can survive an appeal.

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
